transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendez (Oceanic Head of ML), Aisha Roberts (Oceanic VP Eng), Samir Patel (Oceanic SRE), Nora Kim (Product)

Summary: QBR style health check. Looked at month-to-month usage, spikes during promotions (Memorial Day sale), cost drivers (embedding/long context generation), two reliability incidents in last 60 days, roadmap asks (lower p95 latency, SSO + audit visibility), next steps captured.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is the QBR for Oceanic, um we'll go through usage, cost, reliability, and then roadmap items, l'll pass over to Liam for the perf bits in the middle
[00:18] Carlos Mendez: yeah thanks Maya. quick note, appreciate the time, we had a big promo end of May and saw some latency spikes so want to understand root cause and options, thanks
[00:28] Liam O'Neill: cool, yeah i'll start with the reliability recap, so we saw two incidents — one was during the May promo where KV cache thrash caused tail latency to jump, another was a regional networking flapping event, both were mitigated but we want to get you to a place where those don't affect user-facing p95s
[00:45] Aisha Roberts: can you explain KV cash uh cache thrash? we heard "KV cash" in the ops notes and not totally sure what's happening
[00:55] Liam O'Neill: yeah sorry auto transcript there — KV cache, key-value cache for decoder states. what happened was we had a pattern of very bursty long-context requests that invalidated some of the prefix cache and caused regeneration, so more compute per request and higher queueing
[01:20] Samir Patel: that matches our traces, we saw queue depth spike to 18 on one node, p95 jumped to 820ms which is out of our SLO
[01:32] Maya Chen: right, and from Redwood side we recommended a few mitigations — smarter routing to Dedicated pool for promo traffic, temporary vertical scaling for the promo window, and prompt reshaping to reduce unnecessary long-context calls
[01:46] Carlos Mendez: what's the delta in cost if we move more of the promo traffic to Dedicated vs hosted? we saw the token bill double during the sale and it's concerning
[01:56] Maya Chen: good q. short answer: Dedicated gives much more predictable throughput and can reduce unit cost at scale but you have to commit. we'll send a route-level cost model, but ballpark for your traffic profile Dedicated could reduce per-token compute cost by ~25-40% depending on utilization and batching
[02:20] Aisha Roberts: can Redwood do burst capacity? we don't want to over-provision for 3 big promo days a quarter
[02:28] Priya Rao: yes, Dedicated supports configurable burst policies — you can reserve a baseline pool and allow burst to hosted at capped rates or pre-bought burst tokens. that's what we've suggested for other retail customers
[02:40] Carlos Mendez: ok good. another ask, on compliance — we need logs and KMS separation for certain data types, is that supported?
[02:50] Priya Rao: absolutely, Private deployments (VPC + on-prem) give you customer-managed KMS, audit log export, and tighter network controls. For Hosted we offer KMS integration and audit logs but for strict data residency we recommend Private
[03:05] Nora Kim: how long to stand up a Private deployment, like if we decide to go that route?
[03:11] Liam O'Neill: depends on scale and whether you want on-prem vs VPC in cloud. Typical timeline for VPC private is 6–8 weeks for integration and testing, on-prem longer. we can run a scoping poc if you want, low-risk pilot first
[03:27] Carlos Mendez: timeline is important. Q3 holiday roadmap has more ML features, we need to decide by end of July ideally
[03:35] Maya Chen: noted. we'll prioritize the cost model and the SOC2 pack so you can make a go/no-go decision
[03:42] Samir Patel: about the benchmark — i want realistic peak traffic replay, is there a recommended test harness?
[03:48] Liam O'Neill: yes, we usually run a 2-hour blended peak with production traces (we anonymize) to surface p50/p95/p99 latency and tail behaviors. We'll run it with your Dedicated config and a fallback to hosted to compare degradation modes
[04:05] Carlos Mendez: perfect. also we want to look at embeddings spend — seems high for similarity search, any quick wins?
[04:12] Maya Chen: embeddings cost can often be reduced by caching vectors for recent items, lowering vector dimensionality with model/quantization recommendations, and using cheaper embedding variants for non-critical queries. we'll include specific suggestions in the cost export
[04:28] Aisha Roberts: question on observability — our product team wants token-level dashboards and per-route cost drilled down. do you expose that in Console?
[04:35] Priya Rao: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost & latency breakdowns per route/model, and you can export CSVs. There's also a usage alerting rule set you can configure
[04:45] Nora Kim: transcript question, some product names in our notes show Redwood Consoel, haha — that's the console right?
[04:51] Maya Chen: yep, console, good call out.
[04:55] [05:00] Liam O'Neill: quick technical note: for the KV cache issue we think a combination of prefix caching config plus slightly narrower batching will stabilize tail latency without increasing cost significantly
[05:12] Samir Patel: we'll share the three spike days and the traces per Liam's request
[05:18] Carlos Mendez: one more thing — security review with our compliance team is likely next week, we'll need SSO/SAML and detailed audit log samples
[05:26] Priya Rao: i'll push the SOC2 and SSO documentation today and we can schedule a security review call, i can be there as well
[05:33] Maya Chen: alright let's recap next steps — we'll send the detailed cost/usage export and QBR deck, SOC2/security pack, propose benchmark dates, and follow up on Dedicated sizing options
[05:46] Aisha Roberts: thanks everyone, this was helpful
[05:49] Carlos Mendez: thanks, talk soon

Post-meeting notes: agreed to run a 2-hour production-traffic benchmark week of 2026-06-22 (pending Samir availability), Redwood to provide detailed cost breakdown by route, and CSM to loop in security docs and schedule compliance call.

References/Artifacts mentioned: QBR deck (link: https://redwood.co/qbr/oceanic-2026-06), Cost spreadsheet (shared in chat), SOC2 pack (to be shared), benchmark harness details (Liam will share RFC)

End of transcript.
